## Pull request overview

This PR introduces an automatic navigation synchronization mechanism in the Console so that Page/Dashboard create/delete/rename operations propagate into each App’s `navigation[]`, reducing manual navigation tree maintenance.

**Changes:**
- Added `useNavigationSync` hook with immutable navigation-tree utilities and per-app + all-apps sync APIs (with toast + undo).
- Added `NavigationSyncEffect` headless component to auto-detect page/dashboard additions/removals from metadata and sync navigation across all apps.
- Added comprehensive unit tests and adjusted the Console eager import budget; updated the roadmap.

### Reviewed changes

Copilot reviewed 5 out of 5 changed files in this pull request and generated 12 comments.

<details>
<summary>Show a summary per file</summary>

| File | Description |
| ---- | ----------- |
| apps/console/src/hooks/useNavigationSync.ts | Implements navigation tree utilities, sync hook methods, and the metadata-watching auto-sync effect. |
| apps/console/src/__tests__/useNavigationSync.test.tsx | Adds unit tests for utilities, hook behavior, all-app helpers, and `NavigationSyncEffect`. |
| apps/console/src/__tests__/console-load-performance.test.tsx | Updates eager-import budget threshold to account for new import. |
| apps/console/src/App.tsx | Mounts `NavigationSyncEffect` to activate automatic navigation syncing. |
| ROADMAP.md | Records completion of navigation sync service work items. |
</details>

Same as `syncPageCreated`: `syncDashboardCreated` appends unconditionally and can create duplicate dashboard entries if one already exists somewhere in the navigation tree. Add an existence check (recursive) and no-op if already present.

The Undo handler saves `{ ...app, navigation: prev }` where `app` is a stale snapshot captured before the update. If the app schema changes between the sync and the user clicking Undo (e.g., other navigation edits, app settings changes), Undo will overwrite those unrelated fields. Prefer re-loading the latest app schema at undo-time (via `findApp(appName)` / refetch) and only restoring `navigation` on that latest object, or use a patch/update API if available.

Undo has the same stale-snapshot overwrite risk here (`{ ...app, navigation: prev }`). Please restore navigation on top of the latest app schema at undo-time to avoid clobbering concurrent app changes.
Undo has the same stale-snapshot overwrite risk here (`{ ...app, navigation: prev }`). Consider fetching the latest app schema when Undo is clicked and only restoring the `navigation` field.
Undo has the same stale-snapshot overwrite risk here (`{ ...app, navigation: prev }`). Consider re-reading the latest app schema at undo-time and only restoring `navigation` to prevent data loss.

The comment says "Add a page nav item to ALL apps that don't already reference it", but the implementation delegates to `syncPageCreated()` which currently always appends. Either implement the described de-dupe behavior or update the comment to match reality (same applies to the dashboard variant below).

`adapter`, `adapterRef`, and `adapterRef.current = adapter` are currently unused in this component. Consider removing them to avoid dead code / lint warnings, or use them if they’re required for a future-proofed cancellation strategy.

These tests wait for the effect with a fixed `setTimeout(50)`, which can be flaky under load and slows the suite unnecessarily. Prefer `waitFor`/`findBy*` (or polling on `mockSaveItem` calls) so the test waits only as long as needed and fails deterministically when the expected call never happens (same pattern repeats in the other effect tests).

`saveApp()` always calls `refresh()`. In the all-apps helpers and `NavigationSyncEffect`, this results in a full metadata refetch after every single `saveItem` (potentially N apps × M changes). Consider letting callers batch updates (e.g., `saveApp(appName, schema, { refresh: false })` and do one `refresh()` at the end), or making the effect do a single refresh after the loop completes.

`syncPageCreated` appends a new nav item unconditionally. If the app navigation already contains a page with the same `pageName` (e.g., user manually added it earlier, or the effect re-runs after a rollback), this will create duplicate entries. Consider adding a recursive `hasNavigationItem(type, name)` check and no-op when it already exists.
Undo has the same stale-snapshot overwrite risk here (`{ ...app, navigation: prev }`). Restore `navigation` on the latest app schema at undo-time to avoid overwriting unrelated app updates.

Undo has the same stale-snapshot overwrite risk here (`{ ...app, navigation: prev }`). Please base the undo save on the latest app schema (and only change `navigation`) to avoid clobbering concurrent changes.
